newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria unions, bosses agree longer working week.
newsitem.headline: Austria unions, bosses agree longer working week.

text.p: Austrian employers and unions have agreed on a framework for new flexible working hours in a bid to raise the international competitiveness of Austrian industry and increase job security.

The social partners - employers and union representatives - struck a deal late on Monday after months of fruitless talks aimed at extending the working week during busy periods. Time off in lieu during slack spells would balance the increase.

Chamber of Economy President Leopold Maderthaner and union boss Fritz Verzetnitsch, who led the talks, hailed the breakthrough, which increases the working week to a maximum 50 hours over an eight-week period from a rigid 38-40 hours at present.
Over a longer period the working week should not exceed 48 hours and over a year it should generally balance out totally.
"This will help Austrian industry to compete better internationally and goes some way to securing jobs," Maderthaner said.
Verzetnitsch described the deal as a "necessary step".

Collective agreements will continue to regulate the working week in most cases but individual firms can also go it alone. If employers and unions fail to reach a collective agreement in their sector, arbitration will be called in.
Parliament is expected to approve the new labour law in time for it to come in to force on April 1 or May 1.

Earlier this month the government ran out of patience with the social partners' lack of progress in introducing flexible working hours and threatened to step in and shake up labour regulations itself.

"This agreement represents a fair balance between the interests of employers and employees. In addition the social partners have shown their ability to negotiate and find a solution," Chancellor Viktor Klima said.
